items.title: Russian strike on buses kills 33, say officials, as deadly attacks on Ukraine surge
items.description: Ukraine accused Russia of targeting the crowded bus in the frontline city to kill as many civilians as possible.

items.title: US and Lebanon protecting wanted Syrian general, BBC finds
items.description: Bassam al-Hassan is being sheltered in return for information - including about abducted US reporter Austin Tice.

items.title: Most UK diplomats to leave East Jerusalem consulate, Israel says, as Miliband says 'vital services' to remain
items.description: Israel said in September it would act in response to UK sanctions on illegal Israeli settlements in the West Bank.

items.title: Christa Pike now walking after failed US execution, lawyer tells BBC
items.description: A lawyer says the murderer of Colleen Slemmer is moving around her hospital room after surviving two lethal injections.

items.title: Tanker hit by multiple projectiles in Gulf off Qatar, maritime agency says
items.description: Casualties have been reported on the vessel, identified by a maritime intelligence firm as the oil and chemical tanker, Acers.

items.title: Spanish pensioner whose eviction sparked nationwide protests dies
items.description: Maricarmen Abascal, 87, was forcibly removed on a stretcher from her apartment of more than 70 years in September.

items.title: New York court hears arguments in ongoing 9/11 families' lawsuit against Saudi Arabia
items.description: The families allege that men with links to the Saudi government helped those who carried out the 2001 attacks, something the country denies.

items.title: South Korea recalls Ukraine envoy over prisoner-of-war row
items.description: It is the latest in a diplomatic spat after Kyiv disclosed that two North Korean prisoners were transferred to Seoul.

items.title: France's school protests: What lies behind the anger
items.description: Students' blockades and marches spring from real grievances – and from France's habit of settling policy on the street.

items.title: Texas carries out first US execution since Christa Pike's botched lethal injections
items.description: Lawyers for Jamaal Howard had asked a judge to pause the execution after Christa Pike's botched lethal injections.

items.title: Eritrean troops move deep into Ethiopia's Tigray region, residents tell BBC
items.description: Residents of Adigrat tell the BBC they have seen truck loads of soldiers from Eritrea moving south.

items.title: Margaret Hamilton, whose software helped land Apollo 11 on the Moon, dies at 90
items.description: Pioneering computer scientist led the development of the software for Nasa's Apollo mission and was awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom.

items.title: Trump wants a new Camp David-like retreat at his Florida golf club
items.description: Trump's estate would stand in stark contrast to the rustic Camp David and mark another tradition transformed by Trump.

items.title: Former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro expected to face more charges this week
items.description: The new charges are expected to accuse Maduro and his wife of playing a role in the torture of Americans in Venezuelan prisons, US media reports.

items.title: Asahi and Kirin among Japan beer giants raided over alleged price-fixing cartel
items.description: Japan's Fair Trade Commission conducted searches of the country's largest beer-makers.

items.title: Three people killed in Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia airports, officials say
items.description: The Houthis have claimed responsibility for the attacks, which mark an escalation in the conflict.

items.title: Outspoken Indian actor Nana Patekar suddenly dies at 75
items.description: Known for his intense performances, Patekar carved out a distinctive place in Indian cinema.

items.title: Canada suspends plans to expand assisted dying to people with mental illness
items.description: People with mental illness alone were to be eligible for assisted dying in Canada in March 2027, but that has now been paused indefinitely.

items.title: Israelis demand accountability over 7 October failures three years after attacks
items.description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has refused to take any personal responsibility for what happened or order a state inquiry.

items.title: Why Zimbabwe tycoon 'Sir Wicknell' was loved and hated in Africa
items.description: Wicknell Chivayo divided opinion in life and continues to do so in death.
